content_voiceover: This slide, from the Taiwan hemophilia treatment guidelines, shows the frequency of genetic mutations in Taiwanese patients with hemophilia A, pooling data from three studies, Ma, Lin, and Chen. Intron 22 inversion and missense mutations are consistently the two most common mutation types, each accounting for roughly a quarter to over forty percent of cases across the cohorts. Nonsense mutations, deletions, large deletions, insertions, splicing mutations, and intron 1 inversion make up smaller proportions, generally under fifteen percent each. Notably, a portion of patients have no identifiable mutation in the coding DNA, around six to seven percent, which is an important reminder that standard genetic testing can miss deep intronic or regulatory variants. For boards, remember intron 22 inversion is the single most common cause of severe hemophilia A worldwide, and this Taiwanese data mirrors that global pattern.
keypoints: Intron 22 inversion and missense mutations are the most frequent causes of hemophilia A in Taiwan
Distribution parallels global hemophilia A mutation spectrum
Nonsense mutations, deletions, and insertions make up smaller minority shares
A small subset shows no mutation identified in coding DNA
keypoint_voiceover: Key points here. Intron 22 inversion and missense mutations dominate the mutation spectrum in Taiwanese hemophilia A patients. This distribution parallels what's seen globally. Nonsense mutations, deletions, and insertions each contribute smaller minority shares. And a small but notable subset of patients have no mutation identified within the coding DNA, hinting at deeper or regulatory variants.
